column1: # forge model registry — single source of truth for alias resolution.
#   alias    short name you type in --dwarf / --qa
#   harness  which CLI runs it: codex | claude | openclaude | opencode | antigravity
#   model    the exact model id that harness expects
#   effort   which reasoning efforts this pairing accepts, in one of four forms:
#              <=X      any effort on the harness ladder up to and including X
#              a,b,c    exactly these efforts and no others (gaps are real: some
#                       models offer low and high but not medium)
#              none     this model takes no effort flag at all; passing one errors
#              -        harness has no validated ladder; forwarded verbatim
# An effort outside the accepted set is clamped to the nearest lower one that is
# accepted (and reported), rather than failing a dispatch the user already paid
# to start. A word that is not a recognized effort at all is still an error.
# Row order is meaningful: the FIRST row for an alias is that alias's default
# harness. `--dwarf sol` means sol on codex; `--dwarf sol:high:openclaude` moves
# the same model to a different harness.
# An alias with no row here is not an error — it is passed through as a literal
# model id, but only when you name the harness explicitly (forge cannot guess a
# default harness for a model it has never heard of).
# Antigravity (agy). Gemini models take effort as a flag on the UNSUFFIXED id;
# the suffixed ids agy lists (gemini-3.7-flash-low) conflict with --effort.
